mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met in at least two out of the last three tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenues and profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO declines for three months but S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals an inflationary shock met with restrictive policy, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg AND FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in at least 60% of triggered inflation-tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong rebound in housing starts (HOUST) above the prior 12-month high, coincident with rising real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS), signals improved residential demand and construction activity, which boosts materials and homebuilder equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo max AND PAYEMS > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and cost-push inflation, ultimately driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher pricing power for firms.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate revenues and profit expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises for four months but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in at least 70% of such episodes.
